title.narrative: Promoting Nature Positive, resilient and inclusive cities in Lima-Callao, Huancayo and Ica

description.narrative: Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

The project will generate multiple global environmental benefits, contributing to the conservation and sustainable use of biodiversity of local, national, and global significance, the sustained provision of ecosystem services, and climate change mitigation through the conservation, restoration, and promotion of ecosystems and green infrastructure, and the promotion of active mobility, renewable energy, energy efficiency, and waste management in buildings, infrastructure, and neighborhoods. These environmental benefits would not be achieved without GEF funding. In addition, the project will provide significant socioeconomic benefits. In particular, the project will benefit 1,184,424 people (600,477 women, 583,947 men (GEF Core Indicator 11). The project will have health benefits for residents of Lima, Callao, Ica, and Huancayo. Through Outcome 2.1, the project will increase the resilience of residents of Lima and Callao to heat stress, residents of Ica to heat stress and heavy rainfall, and residents of Huancayo to heavy rainfall. Considering the increase in temperature and heat waves in Lima, Callao, and Ica, and the urban heat island effect, the promotion of green infrastructure to regulate temperature will be very valuable, especially for older adults, children, and people with pre-existing heart conditions. Sustainable urban drainage systems (outputs 2.1.4 and 2.1.5) will also provide significant benefits to residents located in flood-prone areas in Ica and Huancayo. Thus, through nature-based solutions, the project will reduce physical injuries, but also the psychological stress resulting from the material and financial losses that heat stress and flooding can cause. The project will also contribute to improving the health of residents of Lima, Callao, Ica, and Huancayo by helping to improve air quality through the promotion of sustainable urban mobility (outputs 2.1.1 and 2.1.3), which will reduce harmful gas emissions, and increasing green infrastructure (directly, component 2), particularly benefiting people with chronic respiratory problems. Similarly, the project will promote active mobility, improving the physical condition of the inhabitants of Ica and Huancayo, and the safety of those who already walk and cycle in these cities. The project will also provide recreational and cultural benefits to residents of the prioritized cities. Through outcome 2.2, and especially outputs 2.2.3 and 2.2.4, the project will contribute to the recovery of ecosystems of cultural value in Lima, Callao, Ica, and Huancayo. In addition, through various outputs, the project will promote the expansion of green infrastructure and the optimization of its management, improving access to quality green areas for the inhabitants of these cities. The project will also provide economic benefits. On the one hand, increased resilience to climate change will reduce the negative financial impacts of heat stress and flooding. Similarly, improving air quality and people's physical condition will reduce sick leave, which is important in contexts where informality prevails, and illness is often associated with loss of income. In addition, the energy efficiency measures promoted in output 1.2.4 will help reduce household expenses for the same consumption. More generally, the project will promote more appropriate financial mechanisms for municipalities, which can benefit households, and will promote investments in sustainable urban development, which will generate green jobs. Finally, the project will contribute to improving urban mobility in Ica and Huancayo, reducing travel time and improving the comfort and safety of travel. As part of the project design, a gender action plan, a stakeholder engagement plan, and a grievance mechanism have been developed to ensure that the project contributes to the socioeconomic well-being of local communities in a culturally appropriate manner. From this perspective, among other aspects, the project will contribute to reducing inequalities and improving women's safety.

To promote sustainable, resilient, low-carbon, and socially inclusive urban development models in Lima, Callao, Ica and Huancayo through integrated planning, sustainable ecosystem management, innovative financial mechanisms, and strategic investments
